# Email Troubleshooting

## Unable to Send Email

If a user cannot send an email, verify that the computer has an
active internet connection.

Check that the recipient's email address is entered correctly.

Verify that the user's email account is connected and authenticated.

Check whether the user's mailbox is full.

If the problem continues, restart the email application and attempt
to send the message again.

## Unable to Receive Email

If a user cannot receive email, verify that the computer has an
active internet connection.

Check whether the mailbox is full.

Verify that the email application is connected to the user's account.

Check the spam or junk folder to determine whether the message was
filtered.

Restart the email application and check for new messages again.

## Email Application Not Working

If the email application is not responding, close and restart the
application.

Verify that the application is up to date.

Restart the computer if the problem continues.

If the application still does not work, determine whether the user
can access their email through the organization's approved webmail
service.

# Network Troubleshooting

## Unable to Access Network Resources

If a computer cannot access a network resource, verify that the
computer has an active network connection.

Confirm that the user has permission to access the requested network
resource.

Check whether other users can access the same resource.

If multiple users cannot access the resource, the problem may be
related to the network service or server.

## Unable to Access Shared Files

If a user cannot access shared files or folders, verify that the
network connection is working.

Confirm that the user has the appropriate permissions for the shared
resource.

Verify that the network path or shared folder location is correct.

If the problem continues, determine whether other users are also
unable to access the shared files.

# Password Reset

## Forgotten Password

If a user has forgotten their password, use the organization's
approved password-reset process.

Verify the user's identity according to the organization's security
procedures before resetting the password.

After the password has been reset, the user should sign in with the
new password.

## Account Locked

If an account has been locked after multiple unsuccessful login
attempts, follow the organization's account-unlock procedure.

Verify the user's identity before unlocking the account.

The user should then attempt to sign in again using the correct
password.

## Password Not Working

If a user's password is not working, verify that the user is entering
the correct username and password.

Check whether Caps Lock is enabled and confirm that the user is using
the current password.

If the password has been forgotten, follow the approved password-reset
process.

# Printer Troubleshooting

## Printer Not Printing

If a printer is not printing, verify that the printer is powered on
and connected to the appropriate network or computer.

Check the printer queue for documents that may be preventing other
jobs from printing.

Verify that the correct printer is selected on the user's computer.

If the printer still does not print, restart the printer and try
printing again.

## Printer Not Responding

If the printer is not responding, check whether the printer is
connected to the network.

Verify that the printer is online and does not display an error
message.

Restart the printer and attempt to print again.

If other users are also unable to print, the problem may be related
to the printer or network rather than the user's computer.

# Software Installation

## Installing Software

Before installing software, verify that the software is approved by
the organization and that the user has permission to install it.

Download the software from the official or organization-approved
source.

Follow the installation instructions provided by the software vendor.

After installation, open the software and verify that it starts
correctly.

## Software Installation Fails

If a software installation fails, verify that the computer meets the
software's system requirements.

Check that the user has sufficient permissions to install software.

Verify that there is enough available storage space on the computer.

If the installation continues to fail, restart the computer and
attempt the installation again.

Check the installation error message for additional information.

## Software Will Not Open

If newly installed software will not open, restart the computer and
try launching the software again.

Verify that the software installation completed successfully.

Check whether the software requires an update.

If the problem continues, reinstall the software using the
organization-approved installation method.

# VPN Troubleshooting

## Unable to Connect to VPN

If a user cannot connect to the VPN, verify that the device has an
active internet connection.

Confirm that the user is entering the correct VPN credentials and
that the appropriate VPN client is installed.

Restart the VPN client and attempt to establish the connection again.

If the VPN still cannot connect, restart the computer and try again.

## VPN Disconnects Frequently

If the VPN connection repeatedly disconnects, check the stability of
the user's internet connection.

A weak or unstable internet connection can cause the VPN connection
to drop.

Restart the VPN client and reconnect to the VPN.

If the problem continues, determine whether other users are
experiencing similar connection problems.

# Wi-Fi Troubleshooting

## Unable to Connect to Wi-Fi

If a computer cannot connect to a wireless network, verify that Wi-Fi
is enabled on the device.

Check that the correct wireless network is selected and that the user
has entered the correct password.

If the device still cannot connect, restart the computer and attempt
to connect again.

If other devices can connect to the network but the affected device
cannot, troubleshoot the affected device's wireless adapter.

## Connected but No Internet

If the computer is connected to Wi-Fi but cannot access the internet,
determine whether other devices on the same network have internet
access.

If multiple devices are affected, the problem may be related to the
network or internet connection.

If only one device is affected, restart the device and reconnect to
the wireless network.
